feedback.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡({t}^{3}+2t),\operatorname{ln}⁡(9-{t}^{2})⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $v.$

$v=⟨${{field-1}}$,\,-\frac{2t}{9-{t}^{2}}\,⟩$
feedback.worked_solution:
The particle's velocity vector is given by the derivative of its position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({t}^{3}+2t)),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(9-{t}^{2}))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3{t}^{2}+2}{{t}^{3}+2t},-\frac{2t}{9-{t}^{2}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
